Lemon juice at the end works if you don't have tamarind.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently on low heat just until hot so the prawns stay tender.

recipes.title: Gujarati Tuvar Dal
recipes.description: Thin, sweet-sour Gujarati dal with toor dal, tomato, jaggery and lemon, studded with peanuts and tempered with mustard, cloves and cinnamon. The everyday dal of a Gujarati thali.

steps.title: Soak dal and peanuts
steps.text: Rinse the toor dal well and soak it with the peanuts for 30 minutes. This helps it cook evenly and softens the peanuts.
steps.visual: Yellow toor dal and pink-skinned peanuts soaking together in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Drain and pressure-cook the dal and peanuts with 450 ml of the water and the turmeric for 4 whistles (about 14 minutes). Let the pressure drop.
steps.visual: Toor dal and peanuts covered with water and a pinch of turmeric in an open steel pressure cooker

steps.title: Whisk and season
steps.text: Whisk the dal smooth and add the remaining water so it's quite thin. Add the tomato, ginger, green chilli, jaggery, salt and chilli powder and simmer for 10 minutes.
steps.visual: Thin, smooth golden dal with tomato pieces, green chilli and whole peanuts simmering in the open pressure cooker

steps.title: Make the tempering
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a small kadai. Add mustard seeds; when they splutter add cumin, fenugreek, cloves, cinnamon, dried red chilli, hing and curry leaves for a few seconds.
steps.visual: Spluttering mustard seeds, cloves, a cinnamon stick, a dried red chilli and curry leaves in ghee in a small iron kadai

steps.title: Pour and finish
steps.text: Pour the tempering into the dal, add the lemon juice and simmer for 2 minutes. Taste — it should be gently sweet, sour and spicy in balance.
steps.visual: The sizzling tempering hitting the golden dal, curry leaves and cloves floating on top

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve with steamed rice, rotli and a dry shaak.
steps.visual: Gujarati dal in a steel katori with peanuts, curry leaves and coriander on top, part of a thali with rice and rotli

substitutions.note: Use a pinch of stevia to keep the khatta-meetha taste without added sugar.
Kokum is traditional; a piece of kudampuli soaked in the dal gives similar sourness.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with a splash of water until bubbling.

recipes.title: Gujarati Cabbage Sambharo
recipes.description: A quick, crunchy Gujarati warm salad-stir-fry of shredded cabbage, carrot and capsicum tossed in a mustard-seed and curry-leaf tempering with a touch of sugar and lemon.

steps.title: Shred the vegetables
steps.text: Finely shred the cabbage, julienne the carrot and slice the capsicum thinly so they cook in seconds.
steps.visual: Fine shreds of pale green cabbage, orange carrot matchsticks and thin green capsicum strips on a wooden board

steps.title: Temper the spices
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide kadai over medium-high heat. Add mustard seeds; when they splutter add hing, curry leaves and green chilli.
steps.visual: Spluttering mustard seeds, curry leaves and slit green chillies in hot oil in a wide black iron kadai

steps.title: Toss on high heat
steps.text: Add all the vegetables with the turmeric, salt and sugar. Toss on high heat for 2 to 3 minutes — they should wilt slightly but stay crunchy.
steps.visual: Shredded cabbage, carrot and capsicum tossed with mustard seeds and curry leaves, lightly yellow and just wilted, in the iron kadai

steps.title: Finish with lemon
steps.text: Turn off the heat and toss with the lemon juice and coriander.
steps.visual: Glistening, crunchy sambharo with fresh coriander in the kadai, a squeezed lemon beside it

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm or at room temperature as part of a Gujarati thali, or alongside dhokla or thepla.
steps.visual: Cabbage sambharo in a small steel bowl, bright orange, green and pale yellow shreds with curry leaves, beside theplas

substitutions.note: Skip the sugar or use a pinch of stevia.
Red or yellow peppers make it more colourful.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 1 day; it softens over time.
recipes.reheating: Serve at room temperature or toss in a hot pan for 30 seconds.

recipes.title: Bharli Vangi (Stuffed Brinjal)
recipes.description: Small brinjals stuffed with a roasted peanut, coconut and sesame masala, sweet-sour with jaggery and tamarind, and slow-cooked until meltingly soft — a Maharashtrian festive favourite.

steps.title: Roast the stuffing base
steps.text: Dry-roast the peanuts in a kadai on medium-low heat for 3 minutes, then add the desiccated coconut and sesame seeds and roast for 2 minutes until golden. Tip out. Add 1 teaspoon of the oil and roast the onion for 5 minutes until browned.
steps.visual: Golden roasted peanuts, coconut and sesame seeds on a plate beside browned sliced onion in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Grind the stuffing
steps.text: Grind the roasted mixture with the garlic, chilli powder, coriander powder, garam masala, turmeric, jaggery, tamarind and salt into a coarse, thick paste, using only a spoon of water.
steps.visual: A coarse, thick, reddish-brown peanut and coconut stuffing paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Slit and stuff the brinjals
steps.text: Keep the stems on. Make two cross slits from the bottom of each brinjal, stopping short of the stem so it stays whole. Soak in salted water for 5 minutes, drain, then press the stuffing generously into the slits. Keep the leftover stuffing.
steps.visual: Small purple brinjals slit into quarters and packed with reddish-brown masala, arranged on a wooden board

steps.title: Temper and arrange
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in the kadai. Add mustard seeds, hing and curry leaves. Arrange the stuffed brinjals in a single layer and cook for 4 minutes, turning gently, so they sear on all sides.
steps.visual: Stuffed brinjals in a single layer searing in the iron kadai with mustard seeds and curry leaves

steps.title: Simmer until soft
steps.text: Mix the leftover stuffing with the water and pour it around the brinjals. Cover and cook on low heat for 15 to 18 minutes, turning once, until the brinjals are completely soft and the gravy is thick.
steps.visual: Soft, glossy stuffed brinjals in a thick, reddish-brown peanut gravy in the covered iron kadai, lid lifted to show steam

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve with jowar or bajra bhakri, or phulka.
steps.visual: Bharli vangi in a steel serving dish, whole stuffed brinjals in thick brown gravy with coriander, a jowar bhakri beside it

substitutions.note: Use cashews for a peanut-free stuffing.
A pinch of stevia or simply leave out the jaggery.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently, covered, with a spoon of water.

recipes.title: Kolhapuri Egg Curry
recipes.description: Boiled eggs in a fiery Kolhapuri-style gravy of browned onion, dry coconut, sesame and whole spices with plenty of red chilli. Bold, hot and very much a Kolhapur dish.

steps.title: Boil the eggs
steps.text: Cover the eggs with water in a saucepan, bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes. Cool in cold water, peel and make 2 or 3 shallow slits in each.
steps.visual: Six peeled, white hard-boiled eggs with shallow slits on a steel plate, a saucepan of water behind

steps.title: Roast the Kolhapuri masala
steps.text: In a dry kadai on low heat, roast the coconut, sesame, dried red chillies, peppercorns and cumin for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant and golden. Add 1 teaspoon of the oil and the sliced onion and roast for 6 minutes until dark brown.
steps.visual: Dark brown roasted onion, golden coconut, sesame and whole red chillies in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Grind the masala
steps.text: Cool the roasted mixture and grind with about 100 ml of the water to a smooth, dark paste.
steps.visual: A smooth, dark reddish-brown Kolhapuri masala paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Fry the eggs
steps.text: Heat the remaining oil in the kadai. Add the eggs with a pinch of turmeric and chilli powder and fry for 2 minutes, rolling them, until lightly blistered. Lift out.
steps.visual: Boiled eggs with a blistered, orange-red spiced skin rolling in hot oil in the iron kadai

steps.title: Cook the gravy base
steps.text: In the same oil, sauté the chopped onion for 4 minutes until golden. Add the ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then the tomato, chilli powder, Kashmiri chilli, coriander powder and salt, and cook for 4 minutes until soft.
steps.visual: A deep red, oily onion-tomato masala in the iron kadai

steps.title: Simmer with the eggs
steps.text: Add the ground masala and fry for 2 minutes. Pour in the remaining water, bring to a boil and add the eggs. Simmer on low for 8 minutes until the gravy is thick with a layer of red oil on top. Stir in the garam masala.
steps.visual: Whole blistered eggs in a thick, fiery red-brown gravy with red oil floating on top in the iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot with bhakri, phulka or rice, with sliced onion and lemon to cool things down.
steps.visual: Kolhapuri egg curry in a steel bowl, halved eggs showing yellow yolks in deep red gravy, topped with coriander, onion slices and lemon beside

substitutions.note: Swap some hot chilli powder for Kashmiri chilli for colour without as much heat.
Fresh coconut works — roast until browned.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Reheat gently with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Bengali Macher Jhol (Rohu Fish Curry)
recipes.description: The light, everyday Bengali fish curry: turmeric-rubbed rohu seared in mustard oil, then simmered with potato wedges in a thin, gingery tomato jhol tempered with kalo jeere.

steps.title: Rub the fish
steps.text: Wash the rohu steaks and pat dry. Rub with half the turmeric and a little salt and leave for 10 minutes.
steps.visual: Rohu fish steaks rubbed bright yellow with turmeric and salt on a steel plate

steps.title: Sear the fish
steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadai until it smokes lightly, then lower the heat a little. Fry the fish in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden. Lift out.
steps.visual: Golden-crusted, turmeric-yellow rohu steaks frying in mustard oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Fry the potatoes
steps.text: In the same oil, fry the potato wedges with a pinch of turmeric for 4 minutes until lightly golden. Lift out.
steps.visual: Long potato wedges turning golden in the same oil in the iron kadai, fried fish on a plate beside

steps.title: Temper and add masala
steps.text: Add the nigella seeds and green chillies to the oil. When the seeds crackle, add the ginger paste, tomato, cumin powder, coriander powder, Kashmiri chilli and the remaining turmeric with 2 tablespoons of water. Cook for 4 minutes until the oil separates.
steps.visual: A loose orange-red masala with crackled black nigella seeds and slit green chillies in the iron kadai

steps.title: Simmer the potatoes
steps.text: Return the potatoes, pour in the water and add salt. Cover and simmer for 10 minutes until the potatoes are almost tender.
steps.visual: Potato wedges simmering in a thin, golden-orange jhol in the iron kadai

steps.title: Add the fish
steps.text: Slide in the fried fish and simmer gently for 5 minutes, spooning the jhol over the pieces rather than stirring, so they stay whole.
steps.visual: Golden rohu steaks and potato wedges in a thin orange jhol with green chillies, gently bubbling in the iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and serve hot with steamed rice and a squeeze of gondhoraj or ordinary lime.
steps.visual: Macher jhol in a white bowl with fish steaks, potato wedges and coriander in a thin orange gravy, a mound of rice and a lime wedge beside it

substitutions.note: Any firm fish works — sear basa for only 1 minute per side.
Winter jhol often uses cauliflower; it also lowers the carbs.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently on low heat, covered.

recipes.title: Shorshe Maach (Bengali Mustard Fish)
recipes.description: Fish in a sharp, creamy paste of freshly ground mustard seeds and green chilli, finished with raw mustard oil. Pungent, simple and quintessentially Bengali.

steps.title: Soak the mustard seeds
steps.text: Soak the mustard seeds in warm water for 20 minutes. This softens them and reduces bitterness.
steps.visual: Black and yellow mustard seeds soaking in a small steel bowl of warm water

steps.title: Grind the shorshe paste
steps.text: Drain and grind the mustard seeds with one green chilli, a pinch of salt and 3 tablespoons of water in short bursts to a smooth, pale yellow paste. Don't grind continuously — heat turns it bitter. Mix in 100 ml of the water.
steps.visual: A smooth, creamy pale-yellow mustard paste in a small mixer jar, a few black seed specks visible

steps.title: Season the fish
steps.text: Rub the fish pieces with the turmeric and a little salt.
steps.visual: Large white fish pieces rubbed yellow with turmeric in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Temper in mustard oil
steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadai until it smokes lightly, then lower the heat. Add the nigella seeds and slit green chillies and let them crackle for a few seconds.
steps.visual: Black nigella seeds and slit green chillies crackling in golden mustard oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Simmer in the paste
steps.text: Pour in the mustard paste and the remaining water and bring to a gentle simmer. Lay the fish in a single layer, cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 minutes until the fish flakes easily. Shake the pan instead of stirring.
steps.visual: Yellow-tinged fish pieces in a creamy mustard-yellow gravy with green chillies in the covered iron kadai, lid slightly lifted

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Drizzle a teaspoon of raw mustard oil over the top and serve with steamed rice.
steps.visual: Shorshe maach in a white bowl, fish pieces under a glossy mustard-yellow gravy with slit green chillies and a sheen of mustard oil, steamed rice beside it

substitutions.note: Rohu or hilsa are traditional; sear the steaks lightly first.
In a pinch, a smooth mustard sauce with a little water saves soaking and grinding, though the flavour is milder.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 1 day; mustard paste can turn bitter if kept longer.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently on low heat, covered.

recipes.title: Cholar Dal with Coconut
recipes.description: Bengal's festive chana dal, slightly sweet and fragrant with whole garam masala, bay leaf and ghee, studded with golden fried coconut bits and a few raisins. The classic partner for luchi.

ingredients.prep: fresh coconut cut into tiny bits

steps.title: Soak and cook the dal
steps.text: Soak the chana dal for 1 hour, then drain and pressure-cook with the water, turmeric and salt for 2 whistles (about 8 minutes). The grains should be soft but still whole, not mushy.
steps.visual: Soaked golden chana dal with water and turmeric in an open steel pressure cooker

steps.title: Fry the coconut
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a kadai over medium heat and fry the coconut bits for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Lift them out with a slotted spoon.
steps.visual: Tiny cubes of fresh coconut turning golden in ghee in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: In the same ghee, add the bay leaves, cumin, dried red chillies, cinnamon, cardamom and cloves and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the ginger paste and green chilli and stir for 1 minute.
steps.visual: Bay leaves, a cinnamon stick, cardamom, cloves and dried red chillies sizzling in ghee with ginger paste in the iron kadai

steps.title: Simmer the dal
steps.text: Pour in the cooked dal, add the sugar, raisins and most of the fried coconut. Simmer for 6 to 8 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.
steps.visual: Thick golden-yellow chana dal with plump raisins and golden coconut bits bubbling in the iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Top with the remaining coconut and serve with luchi, phulka or steamed rice.
steps.visual: Cholar dal in a brass bowl topped with golden coconut bits and raisins, a bay leaf on top, beside a plate of phulkas

substitutions.note: Leave out the sugar and raisins, or use a pinch of stevia, for a less sweet dal.
Use mustard oil for a vegan everyday version.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with a splash of water; it thickens on standing.

recipes.title: Begun Bhaja (Air Fryer)
recipes.description: Thick rounds of brinjal rubbed with turmeric, chilli and salt and air-fried with a brush of mustard oil until creamy inside and golden outside — Bengal's favourite bhaja, without the deep-frying.

steps.title: Slice the brinjal
steps.text: Cut the brinjal into even ½-inch rounds so they cook through without burning.
steps.visual: Even, thick rounds of purple-skinned brinjal laid out on a wooden board

steps.title: Rub with spices
steps.text: Mix the turmeric, chilli powder, sugar and salt and rub it over both sides of each slice. Leave for 10 minutes — the salt draws out moisture.
steps.visual: Brinjal rounds rubbed yellow-orange with turmeric and chilli, beads of moisture on the surface, in a wide steel bowl

steps.title: Brush with mustard oil
steps.text: Pat off excess moisture and brush both sides of each slice with mustard oil.
steps.visual: Spice-rubbed brinjal rounds glistening with a thin coat of mustard oil, a pastry brush beside them

steps.title: Air fry until golden
steps.text: Arrange in a single layer in the air-fryer basket and cook at 190°C for 12 to 14 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and soft right through. In an oven, bake at 220°C for 18 minutes; on a pan, cook over medium heat for 4 minutes per side.
steps.visual: Golden-brown brinjal rounds with crisp edges in a single layer in an open air-fryer basket

steps.title: Serve hot
steps.text: Serve straight away with steamed rice and dal, the way a Bengali meal begins.
steps.visual: Golden begun bhaja rounds on a white plate beside a mound of rice and a bowl of yellow dal

substitutions.note: Neutral oil works if you prefer a milder taste.

recipes.storage: Best eaten fresh.
recipes.reheating: Re-crisp in the air fryer at 180°C for 2 to 3 minutes.

recipes.title: Shukto
recipes.description: A gently bitter-sweet Bengali mixed-vegetable dish of bitter gourd, raw banana, sweet potato, brinjal, drumstick and radish in a light milk and mustard-ginger sauce, traditionally the first course of a Bengali lunch.

steps.title: Cut the vegetables
steps.text: Cut the raw banana, sweet potato, brinjal and radish into 2-inch batons, the drumstick into 2-inch pieces and slice the bitter gourd thinly. Keep the raw banana in water so it doesn't darken.
steps.visual: Neat piles of thin bitter gourd slices, green raw banana batons, orange sweet potato, purple-skinned brinjal, drumstick pieces and white radish batons on a large wooden board

steps.title: Grind mustard and ginger
steps.text: Drain the soaked mustard seeds and grind with the ginger and 3 tablespoons of water to a smooth paste, in short bursts so it doesn't turn bitter.
steps.visual: A small mixer jar with a smooth pale yellow mustard and ginger paste

steps.title: Fry the bitter gourd
steps.text: Heat the mustard oil in a kadai and fry the bitter gourd slices for 3 minutes until lightly browned. Lift out and keep aside.
steps.visual: Thin bitter gourd slices turning golden-brown in mustard oil in a black iron kadai

steps.title: Temper and sauté vegetables
steps.text: Add the ghee to the kadai with the panch phoron and bay leaves. When the seeds crackle, add the raw banana, sweet potato, drumstick and radish with the turmeric and salt and sauté for 4 minutes. Add the brinjal and sauté 2 minutes more.
steps.visual: Batons of raw banana, sweet potato, radish, drumstick and brinjal tossed with crackled panch phoron and bay leaves in the iron kadai

steps.title: Simmer with the paste
steps.text: Stir in the mustard-ginger paste and water. Cover and simmer on low heat for 10 to 12 minutes until the vegetables are just tender but holding their shape.
steps.visual: Mixed vegetable batons simmering in a thin, pale yellow mustard sauce in the covered iron kadai, steam escaping

steps.title: Add milk and bitter gourd
steps.text: Pour in the milk, add the sugar and the fried bitter gourd and simmer uncovered for 4 minutes until the sauce is creamy and lightly thickened. Stir gently so the vegetables don't break.
steps.visual: Vegetables in a creamy, ivory-white milk and mustard sauce with dark bitter gourd slices on top in the iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm with steamed rice as the first course of a Bengali meal.
steps.visual: Shukto in a white bowl, colourful vegetable batons in a creamy pale sauce with a bay leaf, beside a mound of steamed rice

substitutions.note: Use thin coconut milk and skip the ghee for a vegan shukto.
Ash gourd lowers the carbs and suits the light sauce.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently on low heat with a splash of milk; don't boil.

recipes.title: Odia Dalma
recipes.description: Odisha's beloved dal-and-vegetable stew: toor dal simmered with pumpkin, raw banana, brinjal and drumstick, tempered with panch phoron and finished with roasted cumin-chilli powder and coconut.

steps.title: Make bhaja masala
steps.text: Dry-roast the cumin seeds and 2 dried red chillies in a kadai on low heat for 2 minutes until the cumin darkens and smells smoky. Cool and crush to a coarse powder.
steps.visual: Dark-roasted cumin seeds and two blackened dried red chillies in a small dry iron kadai, a little crushed powder in a katori beside

steps.title: Cut the vegetables
steps.text: Cut the pumpkin, raw banana and brinjal into 1-inch cubes and the drumstick into 2-inch pieces.
steps.visual: Orange pumpkin cubes, green raw banana cubes, purple brinjal cubes and drumstick pieces on a wooden board

steps.title: Cook dal with vegetables
steps.text: Put the drained toor dal, all the vegetables, ginger, turmeric, salt and water in a pressure cooker. Cook for 2 whistles (about 8 minutes) so the dal is soft but the vegetables keep their shape. In a saucepan, simmer the dal for 20 minutes first, then add the vegetables for 12 minutes.
steps.visual: Toor dal with pumpkin, raw banana, brinjal and drumstick under yellow-tinged water in an open steel pressure cooker

steps.title: Temper with panch phoron
steps.text: Heat the ghee in the kadai. Add the panch phoron, remaining dried red chillies and bay leaves and let them crackle for 20 seconds. Pour the tempering into the dalma.
steps.visual: Crackling panch phoron seeds, dried red chillies and bay leaves in ghee being poured over the dal in the pressure cooker

steps.title: Simmer and season
steps.text: Simmer the dalma for 3 minutes, stirring gently. Stir in half the roasted cumin-chilli powder.
steps.visual: Thick golden dalma with chunks of orange pumpkin and drumstick, flecked with dark roasted spice, bubbling in the open pressure cooker

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with steamed rice, topped with the grated coconut and the remaining bhaja masala.
steps.visual: Odia dalma in a bell-metal bowl topped with white grated coconut and a dusting of roasted cumin-chilli powder, steamed rice beside it

substitutions.note: Bottle gourd or papaya keep it lighter in carbs.
Mustard oil makes it vegan.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days.
recipes.reheating: Reheat with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Chicken Rezala (Lighter, Kolkata Style)
recipes.description: Kolkata's pale, fragrant Mughlai curry: chicken in a yoghurt, onion and cashew gravy with whole spices, white pepper notes and dried red chillies. Made with milk and modest ghee instead of heavy cream.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Mix the chicken with the curd, ginger-garlic paste and salt. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces coated in a creamy white yoghurt marinade in a steel mixing bowl

steps.title: Make onion-cashew paste
steps.text: Boil the onion in 100 ml of the water for 5 minutes until soft, then grind it with the drained cashews to a smooth, pale paste. Boiling instead of frying keeps the rezala white.
steps.visual: A smooth, ivory-coloured onion and cashew paste in a mixer jar

steps.title: Temper whole spices
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy kadai over medium heat. Add the bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and dried red chillies and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
steps.visual: Whole cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves and dried red chillies sizzling in ghee in a heavy iron kadai

steps.title: Cook the paste
steps.text: Add the onion-cashew paste and cook on low heat for 4 minutes, stirring, until it no longer smells raw. Don't let it brown.
steps.visual: Pale, creamy onion-cashew paste bubbling gently with whole spices in the iron kadai

steps.title: Add the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken with all its marinade and cook on medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring. Add the ground pepper, green chillies, sugar and the remaining water. Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes until tender.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces in a pale, creamy gravy with slit green chillies in the covered iron kadai, lid lifted to show steam

steps.title: Finish with milk
steps.text: Stir in the milk and simmer uncovered for 4 minutes until the gravy is creamy and coats the chicken. Check the salt.
steps.visual: Chicken in a smooth, ivory-white rezala gravy with red chillies and green chillies floating on top in the iron kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes and serve with phulka, paratha or a small portion of pulao.
steps.visual: Chicken rezala in a white ceramic bowl, pale creamy gravy with whole dried red chillies and green chillies on top, phulkas beside it

substitutions.note: Blanched almonds give a similar body.
Mutton rezala is the original; pressure-cook for 20 minutes after adding the meat.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently on low heat with a splash of milk; don't boil hard or the yoghurt may split.

recipes.title: Bhapa Doi (Low-Sugar Steamed Yoghurt)
recipes.description: Bengal's silky steamed yoghurt pudding, set with thick hung curd and milk, scented with cardamom and sweetened lightly with a little sugar instead of a whole tin of condensed milk.

steps.title: Whisk the custard
steps.text: Whisk the hung curd, milk, sugar and crushed cardamom in a bowl for 2 minutes until completely smooth and the sugar has dissolved.
steps.visual: A smooth, thick, creamy white yoghurt mixture in a steel mixing bowl with a whisk and a few crushed cardamom seeds on top

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Pour the mixture into four small steel bowls or ramekins and cover each tightly with foil so no water drips in.
steps.visual: Four small steel bowls filled with smooth white yoghurt mixture, two already covered with foil

steps.title: Steam gently
steps.text: Bring the water to a simmer in a steamer and steam the bowls on low heat for 20 to 25 minutes until set but still slightly wobbly in the centre. In an oven, bake in a water bath at 160°C for 25 to 30 minutes.
steps.visual: Foil-covered steel bowls sitting in a steamer basket over gently simmering water, wisps of steam rising

steps.title: Cool and chill
steps.text: Let the bowls cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours until firm and cold.
steps.visual: Uncovered bowls of set, pale ivory steamed yoghurt with a smooth top, cooling on a rack

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Top with slivered pistachios and serve chilled in the bowls, or run a knife around the edge and turn out onto plates.
steps.visual: A small bowl of silky bhapa doi with a smooth ivory top sprinkled with green pistachio slivers, a spoon beside it

substitutions.note: Use stevia to taste for a sugar-free version; the texture stays the same.
Use nolen gur (date-palm jaggery) or regular jaggery for a winter-style bhapa doi.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate covered up to 3 days.
